description: Nutrition information for Slivered Almonds

title: Sicilian Olive Salad
description:
This cracked olive medley is a family favorite that is popular both in Calabria and Sicily. Sicilian Castelvetrano olives are becoming readily available in major supermarkets now, and if you have access to those, they are a great choice for this salad. Many Italian-American delis sell “Sicilian Colossal” olives, which also work well. You can toss a few tablespoons of this mixture into hot pasta in the winter, or chilled rice or quinoa in warner weather. It's also a great way to dress up ordinary vegetables, seafood, and meat.

This recipe comes from The Mediterranean Diabetes Cookbook.
ingredients: 1/2 lbs large green olives (rinsed well, drained, and rubbed dry)
steps: Place olives on a cutting board. Cover with a clean kitchen towel and smash them lightly with a meat hammer or the back of a skillet. (The objective is to slightly crush the olives.)
Place olives in a bowl and stir together with remaining ingredients.
Marinate salad for an hour at room temperature, or cover and chill in refrigerator for at least 1 day and up to 3 days. Bring salad to room temperature before serving.

title: Yogurt Ranch Dressing
description: Nothing beats homemade, including ranch dressing! Creamy yogurt adds protein but fresh herbs are the star in this diabetes-friendly salad dressing.
steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, chives, parsley, garlic, onion powder, dried dill, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Allow the dressing to sit in the refrigerator for at least 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Walnuts, whole
description: Nutrition information for walnuts

title: Shrimp and Avocado Taco Bowls
description: Cooked shrimp is an easy short cut, or you can use leftover shrimp and keep it in the fridge overnight. The pineapple and avocado add a bright, fresh flavor to these easy taco bowls.
serving_size: 1 lettuce bowl + 4 oz shrimp + about 1/2 cup pineapple and avocado
ingredients: 1/2 lbs fully cooked shrimp (peeled, deveined, tails removed)
steps: Combine the shrimp, avocado, tomato, scallions, and pineapple (and jalapeño, if desired). Remove a few of the central leaves from each lettuce head to make a bowl. Divide the shrimp mixture between the lettuce heads.
Stir the chili powder into the Greek yogurt.
Top each “taco” bowl with the Greek yogurt mixture and salsa. Sprinkle chopped fresh cilantro on top, if desired.

title: California Date and Acorn Squash Salad
description: The sweetness of the California Dates pairs beautifully with the spiciness of the arugula and the Indian spice blend, garam masala, adds depth of flavor to this enticing side dish. Keeping the skin on the acorn squash adds texture and fiber to the dish as well. Feel free to swap out the acorn squash with other winter varieties, such as delicata squash.
ingredients: 1 whole acorn squash (sliced into ½-inch thick slices)
3/4 cup California dates (pitted and cut into quarters)
1/3 cup toasted nuts of choice (such as pistachios, pecans, walnuts, or almonds)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment paper.

In a large bowl, add squash, oil, ½ teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon garam masala and mix together well. Place the squash on the baking sheet in a single layer and roast for 20 minutes, turning over pieces halfway.
In same bowl, add juice, jam, ground black pepper, and remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon garam masala. Whisk together well.
Add cooked squash and dates to bowl and toss together.
Place arugula in a large serving bowl or platter. Add squash and dates. Top with toasted nuts.

title: Roasted Veggie Strata
description: This egg-based entrée is great any time of the day and the leftovers can be an easy grab-and-go lunch for the next day.
ingredients: 1 med sweet potatoes (6-ounce, peeled and diced)
1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
8 slice whole wheat bread (1.5 ounce each)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Coat a large baking sheet with cooking spray.
Toss all of the vegetables together and spread evenly on the baking sheet. Spray the vegetables with 5-6 sprays of cooking spray and season with salt-free Spike seasoning.
Roast the vegetables for 30 minutes, then set aside to cool slightly.
Whisk together the eggs, egg whites, dried mustard, sage, and black pepper.

Coat a 9x13-inch casserole dish with cooking spray. Tear four pieces of the whole wheat bread into pieces and layer them on the bottom of the casserole dish. Top with 1/2 the roasted vegetables and 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese. Pour half the egg mixture over the bread, vegetables, and cheese.

Repeat the layering process with the remaining torn bread, vegetables, cheese, and egg mixture. Press down on the casserole with a spatula to ensure all of the bread soaks in the egg mixture. Let the strata sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Bake the strata for 30 minutes.
To serve, cut the strata down the middle lengthwise, then cut down the middle width-wise. Cut each half down the middle width-wise again to make 8 equal servings.

title: Gingered Pumpkin Bisque
description: This sweet and savory soup combines pumpkin, pear, and fresh ginger into a creamy soup that will warm you up on a chilly fall day. You can toss everything in a slow-cooker and let it cook all day, so dinner is ready when you come home from work. Pair this dish with an Arugula, Pear, Walnut, & Pecorino Salad for a fall-themed soup-and-salad combo or Tarragon Herbed Chicken and Mushrooms for something heartier.
ingredients: 1 med firm pear (peeled, cored, and chopped)
1 (14.5-oz) can low sodium chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Coat a 3 ½ - to 4-quart slow cooker with cooking spray. Add the pumpkin, pears, onions, broth, cumin, nutmeg, salt, and cayenne to the slow cooker. Cover and cook on high for 3 ½ hours, or on low for 7 hours, or until onions are tender.

Working in 1-cup batches, purée the pumpkin mixture in a blender, being sure to secure the lid tightly while blending. Return the mixture to the slow cooker, stir in the remaining ingredients, except the yogurt. Cover and cook on high for 30 more minutes.
Serve topped with 1 tbsp of yogurt.

title: Grilled Strawberries on “Crème” with Balsamic Glaze
description: This diabetes-friendly recipe for grilled strawberries on crème with balsamic glaze is sure to impress! Utilizing natural sweeteners like maple syrup or honey includes extra nutrients. The Greek yogurt adds some extra protein to help keep you feeling satisfied after eating this delicious dessert. This is also a great choice if you are looking for gluten-free or vegetarian sweet treat.
serving_size: ½ plate (9 strawberry halves + 1/3 cup creme)
ingredients: 1 tbsp light cream cheese (at room temperature)
1 tbsp balsamic glaze or balsamic reduction sauce*
1 tbsp extra small fresh basil or mint leaves
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together the yogurt, Neufchâtel, and honey until thick and creamy. Spread the crème onto a serving platter or board.
Prepare and preheat a grill or grill pan. Brush the cut side of the strawberry halves with the oil and grill over direct medium-high heat, cut-side down, until rich grill marks form, about 4 minutes.
Arrange the strawberries on the crème. Drizzle with the balsamic glaze, sprinkle with the almonds and fresh herbs, and serve.

*Make your own balsamic reduction sauce: Add 1/4 cup balsamic vinegar to a small saucepan, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring a couple times, until it can just coat the back of a spoon (to yield about 1 1/2 tablespoons), about 5 minutes. (Note: The balsamic reduction thickens slightly as it cools.)

title: Grilled Corn with Chili and Lime
description: Enjoy some Tex-Mex flair with this Grilled Corn with Chile and Lime. Tasting like Mexican street corn, this diabetes-friendly recipe is flavorful and nutritious.
steps: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, chili powder, smoked paprika, lime zest, lime juice and salt.
Brush the ears of corn with the marinade, making sure to coat them evenly.
Allow the corn to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Place the marinated corn on the preheated grill. Grill for about 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until the corn is charred and cooked through.
Remove the grilled corn from the heat.
Transfer the corn to a serving platter and sprinkle with cotija and fresh chopped cilantro.

title: Sheet Pan Zucchini and Red Pepper "Stir-Fry"
description: This recipe looks and tastes like a stir-fry, but it is roasted in the oven instead of cooking it on the stovetop. Just toss everything together, lay it out on a sheet pan, and let it bake! It's great as is, or you could add some additional flavors: Sprinkle with peanuts for crunch; drizzle with hot sauce for pow; add fresh cilantro for herbal flair.
ingredients: 2 med red bell pepper (cut into 1-inch strips)
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp lower sodium soy sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with unbleached parchment paper.
Pat or squeeze the tofu of excess liquid, if necessary. Cut the tofu into (3/4-inch) cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk together the ginger, tamari, vinegar, and oil. Add the zucchini and bell pepper pieces to the sauce mixture; toss by hand to coat.
Arrange the zucchinis and peppers in a single layer on the baking sheet (fill 2/3 of the sheet), letting excess sauce drip back into the bowl.
Add the tofu to the bowl with the remaining sauce mixture; toss to coat. Arrange the tofu in a single layer on the baking sheet (fill the rest of the sheet). Drizzle tofu with any remaining sauce.
Roast until the tofu and vegetables are browned, about 30 minutes; no stirring needed. Serve.

title: Green Chili Chicken Casserole
description: This Green Chili Chicken Casserole is a crowd-pleaser, and the combination of green chilies, chicken, and cheese creates a comforting and delicious dish. It’s perfect for an easy weeknight dinner the whole family can enjoy.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans (no salt added, rinsed and drained)
3/4 cup shredded Mexican cheese blend (low fat)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Spray a 9-inch square baking dish with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, combine chopped chicken, black beans, diced green chilies, red bell pepper, Greek yogurt, salsa verde, ground cumin, garlic powder, and black pepper. Mix until well combined.
Spoon the chicken mixture into the baking dish, spreading it out evenly.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the top.
Cover the casserole with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake until the casserole is hot and bubbly and the cheese is melted and golden brown, about 10 minutes more.
Remove from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing into 8 squares. Top with chopped, fresh cilantro.

title: Smoky Mushrooms
description: Cooked mushrooms boost up the savory flavor of a burger or steak. They are also a perfect side dish for roasted pork loin or grilled tofu. You can use white, crimini (baby bella), shiitake or oyster mushrooms in this recipe – or a blend of different varieties. If you’re using shiitake mushrooms, remove and discard the entire stem.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper; set aside.
Trim the stems of the white mushrooms. Slice the mushrooms into 3/8-inch-thick pieces. Add the mushrooms to a bowl. Add the remaining ingredients and toss well. The mixture will look dry.
Spread the mushrooms in a single layer on each sheet. Roast for 10 minutes. Flip the mushroom slices and roast for 10 minutes more.
Increase the heat to 375°F and roast for 15 minutes. Flip the mushroom slices again and continue to roast for 10 minutes more. Serve as a side dish, or add to sandwiches, omelets, and soups.

title: Sweet Potato and Spinach Dumplings
description: Savory sweet potato dumplings are surrounded by a meaty tomato sauce in this restaurant-worthy main dish.
ingredients: 1 cup fat-free, reduced sodium ricotta cheese
1/2 cup frozen spinach (chopped, thawed and drained)
1 marinara sauce (24.5-ounce jar, light-in-sodium (such as Amy’s))
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Place the sweet potato on a baking sheet and bake for 40 minutes, or until soft when poked with a fork. Remove the sweet potato from the oven and set it aside to cool.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk the egg, egg whites, and cottage cheese until smooth. Fold in the Parmesan cheese, pepper, nutmeg, and spinach.
Remove the skin from the sweet potato and mash well. Fold in the mashed sweet potato and the flour to the egg-cheese mixture. The mixture will be wet and sticky. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
While the dough rests, coat a large sauté pan or Dutch oven with cooking spray and heat it over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and sauté until barely cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Pour the marinara sauce and broth over the turkey and stir to incorporate. Reduce the heat to low.
Scoop 2-inch balls of the dumpling batter and gently drop them into the sauce to make 24 dumplings. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.

title: Red Onion Green Beans
description: Fresh green beans cooked for just a few minutes have a delicate crunch and bright flavor. With fresh thyme and sauteed red onions this side dish will become a favorite.
ingredients: 2 med red onion (halved, peeled, and sliced 1/2 inch thick)
steps: Bring a 6-quart pot of water, filled 2/3 full, to boiling. Add the salt. Add the green beans and turn off the heat. Let the green beans stand in the water for 3 to 4 minutes. Drain. Plunge the green beans into a bowl of ice water. Drain the beans; set aside.

In a large skillet, heat the butter and oil over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 to 25 minutes, until very soft. Lower the heat if the onions begin to brown too quickly.

Add the thyme and green beans to the onions and heat through, using tongs to gently turn the vegetables. To serve, place the onion–green bean mixture on a platter and top with the almonds and lemon zest.

title: Shrimp Ceviche
description: This version of ceviche features savory shrimp, sweet pineapple, and hot chilis in a tangy lime marinade. Serve on top of cooked rice and peas or as a salsa over cooked fish. Or, serve with crackers as a snack or appetizer.
steps: Place mixture in a serving bowl and add the chopped shrimp and olive oil. Chill for 30 minutes or more before serving

In a food processor, add green onions, tomato, peppers, pineapple, and cilantro; pulse on-off button to chop to a very coarse consistency. Chunky texture is desired. Add lime juice, vinegar and garlic powder to the mixture.

title: Kale Apple Slaw
description:
You can switch up the vegetables in this slaw by using chopped spinach, green cabbage, and shredded carrots.

Complete your plate: Pair this vegetable side side with Easy Beef Chili. Both are great as leftovers, so this is makes a great meal-prep meal
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, garlic, mustard, olive oil, lemon juice, water, salt, and black pepper.
Add the kale, cabbage, and apple to the bowl and toss to evenly coat. Cover and place in the refrigerator for 30 minutes before serving for the flavors to combine.

title: Almost Smooth Salsa
description: Are you a smooth or chunky salsa lover? If you like your salsa smooth, then blend until smooth. If you like your salsa chunky, then skip the blending altogether.
ingredients: 1/2 whole jalapeño pepper (seeded, veins removed, diced)
steps: Add the tomatoes, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño, and cilantro to a medium bowl. Add the lime juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Toss to evenly coat.
Using an immersion blender, blend until almost smooth, leaving some chunks in the salsa.

title: Parsley and Cilantro Chimichurri Baked Cod
description: Zesty chimichurri sauce made from parsley, cilantro, vinegar, and lime top the mild cod. This diabetes-friendly protein dish comes together quickly and is easy to make by baking it in the oven. Try making cilantro lime quinoa for a tasty side starch to pair with it.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Place the cod filets on a parchment paper lined baking sheet. Lightly drizzle with 1 tbsp oil. Place the baking sheet in the oven and cook until the internal temperature of the fish is 145°F, 8–10 minutes.
Place the garlic, onion, parsley, cilantro, crushed red pepper, and black pepper in a food processor. Process until finely chopped.
Add vinegar, lime zest and juice, and 3 tbsp olive oil. Process until smooth and set aside.
To serve, divide fish between plates and top with chimichurri sauce.

title: Cashews 1/2 ounce
description: Nutrition information for cashews

title: Roasted Baby Carrots
description: Roasting brings out the natural flavor and sweetness in these carrots. We used parsley here, but you could use other fresh herbs like tarragon, dill, mint, thyme, rosemary, or a combination.
ingredients: 1 tbsp honey or 2 packets artificial sweetener
1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley or 1 tsp dried parsley
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
In a small bowl, mix together the carrots and olive oil. Pour the mixture onto the baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until the carrots are tender.
Place the carrots into a bowl and mix with the honey or artificial sweetener. Sprinkle the carrots with parsley or other herbs.

title: Lightly Salted Pistachios
description: Nutrition information for 50 lightly salted pistachios

title: Roasted Red Pepper Coulis
description: A coulis is simply a thick puree or sauce. This one makes a beautiful and tasty finishing touch for your dishes. (Pictured here with Rosemary Balsamic Onions and Pesto.)
steps: Place whole peppers directly on a grill or gas burner or under your broiler. Roast until they are completely blackened on the outside. Place in a bowl and cover tightly with plastic wrap for at least 15 minutes. Once cooled, you can peel away the blackened skin.
Place the roasted pepper in the food processor and purée until fine.

title: Scallop Kebabs
description: Here’s a totally different way to prepare scallops. Most recipes will have you pan sear them, but why not try something new. I coat the scallops with crunchy panko crumbs seasoned with some Parmesan and garlic and thread them up into kebabs. Under the broiler, the outside gets crisp and the inside of the scallop stays silky.
ingredients: 3 clove garlic (very finely minced, almost to a paste)
12 oz large sea scallops (fresh or frozen, thawed and patted dry)
1 spray, 0.25 g Olive oil cooking spray
steps: Add the wooden skewers to a pan of hot water. Set aside for 1–2 hours.
Cover a broiler pan with aluminum foil. Coat the foil with cooking spray. Preheat the oven broiler to high with the rack set about 5 inches from the heat source.
Combine the breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and Italian seasoning together on a plate. Roll each scallop in the breadcrumb mixture.
Remove the wooden skewers from the hot water. Using two skewers per kebab, thread the scallops onto the skewers so the scallops are lying flat through the skewer.
Place the skewers on the prepared broiler pan. Coat each skewer with olive oil cooking spray. Broil the scallops for about 4 minutes per side until cooked through.

title: Cowboy Bean Fritters
description: Bring this appetizer to share at your next summer barbeque. Serve the fritters with some dipping options like salsa and non-fat plain Greek yogurt (a healthier substitute for sour cream).
ingredients: 2 can black beans (16-ounce, rinsed and drained)
1 tbsp vegetable oil (plus extra if needed)
steps: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add egg whites and salsa; mix well, then stir in black beans.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 Tbsp. oil. Pour 1 Tsp. batter per fritter into skillet, cooking several fritters at one time, but not overcrowding them. Cook 1 minute, then turn fritters and lightly flatten with a spatula; cook 1 to 2 additional minutes or until browned on both sides. Repeat with remaining batter, adding more oil as necessary.

title: Steamed Broccoli
description: Nutrition information for Steamed Broccoli
steps: Place frozen broccoli florets in a microwave-safe bowl.
Add 2–4 tablespoons of water.
Cover the bowl with a microwave-safe plate or lid.
Microwave on high for 2–4 minutes until tender.
Remove carefully, as steam will be hot.

title: Classic Italian Marinara with Whole Wheat Pasta
description: You can make your own marinara sauce at a fraction of the price of commercially bottled sauces. This sauce relies heavily on garlic, but feel free to temper this assertive flavor if you wish. Either cut back on the amount of garlic or slice the garlic instead of mincing it. The more you chop or mince garlic, the more pungent your final dish will be. Larger pieces of garlic, while still flavorful, will release a more subtle taste. This sauce freezes great. Pour into a heavy zip-locked freezer bag and store for up to 6 months.
ingredients: 1 (28-ounce) can canned tomatoes (good-quality, preferably packed in its own juice, drained, reserve liquid)
5 leaves fresh basil (sliced, or you may leave whole)
10 oz Whole wheat pasta (penne, shells, fusilli)
2 tbsp Parmesan or Romano cheese (freshly grated)
steps: Heat the olive oil and garlic in a large skillet with a lid over low heat (do not use a deep pot, you want the water to quickly evaporate and the sauce to become thick). Cook the garlic for about 6-7 minutes, but do not brown, stirring occasionally.

Meanwhile, add the drained tomatoes to a deep bowl. Crush the tomatoes with your hands until coarse. Add the tomatoes and basil to the skillet and simmer for 20-25 minutes until thick. Add some of the reserved liquid from the can of tomatoes, if necessary, if the sauce is too thick.

Meanwhile bring a 3-5-quart pot of lightly salted water (fill the pot 2/3 full) to a rolling boil. Add the pasta and stir for the first minute. Continue to cook the pasta approximately 7-8 minutes until al dente. Drain, do not rinse.

Add in the salt, pepper, and crushed red pepper, if using, to the tomato sauce. Add the pasta to the sauce, cover, and let the pasta sit in the sauce for 1-2 minutes. Add the pasta to a warmed bowl and sprinkle with cheese. (The sauce can also be frozen. Freeze in a quart container and store for 3-4 months.)

title: Bruschetta-Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Bruschetta is a colorful and delicious appetizer for any gathering. For a lower carb option, try this simple bruschetta stuffed in mushrooms instead of serving it on the traditional baguette. This recipe can be found in The Diabetes Superfoods Cookbook and Meal Planner.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Cut tomatoes into quarters and set aside.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and add garlic. Saute garlic for about 1 minute. Add tomatoes and continue to saute for about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in basil and both cheeses.
Remove stems from mushrooms and fill with tomato mixture. Bake in oven for 15 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then drizzle with balsamic vinegar. Serve warm.

title: Gluten-Free Chocolate Banana Muffins
description: Try to use a gluten-free baking mix that lists brown rice flour as the first ingredient to increase your whole-grain intake.
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose Gluten-Free Baking Mix ((such as King Arthur Baking Mix))
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line muffin tins with muffin papers and spray the papers with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, mix together the oil, sugar substitute, and vanilla. Add the bananas and eggs one at a time. Mix well.
Stir in the baking mix, oats, cocoa powder, and water.
Spoon the batter into 12 muffin cups. Top each muffin with mini chocolate chips (distribute evenly over all muffins.)
Bake for 20-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and let the muffins cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Remove the muffins from the pan and cool completely on a wire rack.

title: Radish Toasts with Whipped Ricotta & Chives
description: If you are a fan of avocado toast, mix things up with this radish toast! Diabetes-friendly and filling, this recipe is great to serve as breakfast or brunch.
steps: Toast the bread under the broiler or in a toaster.
Place the ricotta cheese and chives (reserve some chives for garnishing) in a blender or food processor and purée until smooth. Set aside.
Carefully slice (using a mandolin if you have one) the radishes into ⅛ thick rounds.
Divide the cheese and chive mixture between the 4 slices of bread and smooth into an even layer.
Top the cheese with slices of radishes and any extra chopped chives. Sprinkle with pepper if desired.

title: Whole wheat pita
description: Nutrition information for whole wheat pita

title: Roasted Asparagus with Parmesan
description: Asparagus is one of the first green veggies to start popping up in early spring. Here is a simple recipe that lets those spears shine! They’re seasoned with pepper and lemon zest, then finished with fresh lemon juice and a dusting of parmesan
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Snap the tough ends off of the asparagus and discard.
In a large bowl, toss the asparagus with the olive oil, pepper and lemon zest.
Place the asparagus on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer. Bake for 15 minutes or until tender. Remove from the oven, then sprinkle with cheese and lemon juice.

title: Cinnamon Maple Grilled Peaches
description: Who said desserts can’t be grilled? Try dressing up this simple dish by garnishing it with some fresh mint leaves.
ingredients: 4 peaches or nectarines (still firm but ripe)
steps: Cut peaches in half and remove the seed. Place peach halves in a resealable plastic bag.
Mix the lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and maple syrup in a small bowl. Pour the mixture over the peaches in the bag. Seal the bag and turn to coat the peaches.
Preheat grill to medium high. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until golden brown on the outside, and just warmed through inside.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Chia Seed Pudding
description: This pudding is decadent enough to be a fancy dessert for two, or light enough for breakfast or a midday snack. Chia seeds are a diabetes superfood. They are high in fiber and omega-3 fatty acids—great for blood glucose (blood sugar) management and heart health. When combined with liquid, they form a gel creating a pudding-like texture. To make this vegan, use a non-dairy milk like almond or soy.
ingredients: 1 cup skim milk or unsweetened almond milk
steps: Mix cocoa powder, low- or no-calorie sweetener, and powdered peanut butter together, and incorporate well so there are no lumps.
Stir in the chia seeds and stir well to combine.
Whisk in the milk and vanilla. Let sit for 5 minutes, then whisk again. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

title: Unsweetened Dried Cherries, 2 tbsp
description: Nutrition information for 2 tbsp of unsweetened dried cherries

title: Pesto Pasta Tuna Salad
description: This herby pasta salad gets an extra boost with a pantry staple, tuna. No-salt-added albacore tuna helps keep the sodium content down and allows the pesto and vegetables to shine through. Albacore tuna has a firm texture like chicken breast and a mild flavor.
serving_size: 2 cup pasta salad + 2 oz tuna + 2 cups mixed greens
ingredients: 2 (4.5 oz) cans tuna packed in water (solid, no salt added, drained)
steps: Cook the pasta according to the package directions to the al dente stage.

While the pasta is cooking, place the chopped kale in a large bowl and drizzle it with olive oil. Gently rub the oil into the pieces of kale until they soften slightly and turn dark green. Add the zucchini, pepper, and tomatoes to the bowl and toss.

Once the pasta is done, drain it and add it to the vegetables and toss well. Stir in the pesto until the pasta is coated. Cover it tightly and place it in the refrigerator to chill for at least an hour.
Just before serving, gently break apart the tuna and mix it into the pasta and vegetables, coating it with pesto.
Place 2 cups of mixed greens on a plate or a bowl. Top with 2 cups of the pesto pasta tuna.

title: Maple-Thyme Roasted Brussels Sprouts
description: These low-sodium roasted Brussels sprouts are a simple, flavorful side dish. Roasting brings out their natural sweetness, while maple syrup and thyme add a flavor boost.
steps: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts. Add them to a medium bowl.
Remove the thyme leaves from the stems and add them to the bowl.
Add the garlic, olive oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper to the bowl and toss to combine.
Spread the sprouts out in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast in the oven until they are fork-tender and beginning to brown, 20–25 minutes.

title: Tuna Salad Stuffed Tomato Melts
description: A tuna melt with no bread? Of course! A tomato stuffed with savory tuna salad with a bit of melted cheese on top is a filling and delicious lower carb alternative.
ingredients: 2 (5-ounce) cans tuna packed in water (chunk-light, drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to broil (500°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil (spritz with baking spray) and set aside
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and carefully cut around the inner edge to release the core. Use a spoon to remove the seeds and membrane of the tomatoes to create hollow tomatoes.
In a medium bowl, combine tuna, mayonnaise, celery, shallot, and celery salt.
Stuff tomatoes with the tuna mixture and top with a slice of cheese.
Place tomatoes on the baking sheet and broil for 3–5 minutes, until the cheese melts and begins to brown.

title: Spicy Greens and Roasted Red Pepper Shakshuka
description: This classic veggie-packed and fiber-filled Mediterranean breakfast has a smokey, spicy flavor that will get your morning off to a great start and keep you feeling full all morning. Serve it with a slice of whole grain toast on the side.
serving_size: 1 ¼ cup vegetable mixture + 1 poached egg
ingredients: 1 cup yellow onion (diced, about ½ medium onion)
2 (14.5 oz) cans diced tomatoes (no salt added)
steps: In a large (10-inch) cast iron skillet, sauté onions over medium heat until softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Increase the heat slightly and add the eggplant. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Allow the eggplant to brown slightly.
Stir in the tomatoes, water, red pepper, and spices. Bring to a low boil. Stir in the kale and spinach and allow the greens to wilt.
Make 4 wells in the vegetable mixture. Crack the eggs one at a time and place them each in a separate cup or small bowl. Gently place each egg in a well in the vegetable mixture.
Cover the shakshuka and allow the eggs to poach until the yolks are firm, about 10–12 minutes.
Serve with chopped parsley if desired.

title: Vanilla Chia Mini Pudding
description: This quick, no cook chia pudding blends creamy almond milk with warm vanilla for a lightly sweet, smooth base. The chia seeds thicken into a soft, spoon able texture, making this a simple, nutrient-rich snack or breakfast starter you can stir together in minutes.
steps: In a small bowl or jar, combine 2 tablespoons chia seeds, 1/2 cup almond milk, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla.
Stir well to make sure the chia seeds are evenly distributed.
Let the mixture sit for 2–3 minutes, then stir again to prevent clumping.
Enjoy immediately for a looser texture or refrigerate for a thicker pudding.

title: Slow-Cooker Beef Stew
description: Searing beef on the stovetop adds a few minutes to your slow cooker routine, but it’s well-worth the payoff in flavor. Serve this stew with a side of steamed green beans for a balanced weeknight meal that makes your kitchen smell inviting all day long.
ingredients: 1 lbs beef stew meat (visible fat trimmed and cut into 1-inch cubes)
steps: Place the flour in a large resealable plastic bag. Add beef and toss to coat.
Add oil to a pan over high heat. Add beef and sauté for 6-8 minutes, turning frequently until evenly browned.
Transfer beef and all remaining ingredients to a large slow cooker.
Cover and cook in slow cooker on low for 8 hours.

title: Air Fryer Smoky Herb Chicken Tenders
description: Take your chicken dinner to the next level with this smoky, herby chicken tender recipe. Air frying chicken keeps them moist and delicious, plus makes it a quick and easy dinner to make.
ingredients: 1 lbs chicken tenderloins (boneless, skinless, cut in half)
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 400 degrees F, or an oven to 420 degrees F
Combine paprika, cumin, dried oregano, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl.
Lightly spray the tenders with oil, then rub the spice mixture all over the chicken. For best results, let it marinate for at least 20 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Add the chicken to an air fryer basket or a baking tray (lined with parchment or foil).
Air fry for 12–15 minutes or bake for 16–20 minutes until the chicken is 165 degrees F internally.

title: Spinach, Tomato and Feta Cheese Baked Egg
description: If you like to wake up with a hearty egg breakfast, you’ll love this quick and easy recipe.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Spray 4 ramekins with cooking spray. Combine the spinach, tomato, feta cheese, and oregano; evenly distribute into ramekins..
Place egg over spinach mixture and bake until egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft, about 10-12 minutes

title: Parmesan Mashed Cauliflower
description: Trade out mashed potatoes for this low-carb copycat! Cauliflower easily replaces potatoes in this flavorful side dish.
ingredients: 1 head cauliflower (trimmed and cut into florets, about 4 cups)
steps: Place the cauliflower florets in a microwave-safe dish and microwave for about 8 minutes, until the cauliflower is soft. Stir halfway through the cooking time.
Place the cauliflower, yogurt, cheese, garlic powder, and pepper in a food processor or blender and blend until smooth,
Top with the onions and serve.

title: Unsalted Almond Butter
description: Nutrition information for 2 Tbsp Unsalted Almond Butter

title: Simply Spiced Shrimp
description: A simple spice blend adds a burst of flavor to shrimp. Cook these up and store them in the fridge or freeze and then add them to tacos, salads or wraps.
steps: In a bowl, mix together the shrimp, garlic, paprika, and chili powder, tossing to coat. Add 1 tsp. of the olive oil and the lemon juice. Let stand 3 minutes.
In a large skillet, heat the remaining 2 tsp. oil over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp and sauté on both sides for a total of 3 minutes, or until the shrimp is just opaque and cooked through.

title: Braised Herbed Chicken
description: Need a quick, easy and healthy dinner? This is the meal for you. It only takes a few minutes to prepare and then simmers for 30 minutes for a delicious flavor that will have your house smelling delightful too.
ingredients: 2 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, reduced sodium)
steps: In a small bowl, combine the rosemary, thyme, oregano, garlic powder and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and sauté for 3 minutes per side.
Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and carrots around the chicken in the pan. Pour the herb mixture over the chicken and potatoes.
Add the chicken broth to the pan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer; cover and cook for 30-35 minutes.

title: California Date & Cashew Chicken Stir Fry
description: This easy chicken stir fry pairs well with the sweetness from California Dates and a touch of heat from red pepper flakes. For a spicier dish, chop up a fresh chili pepper and add it with the scallions. Pair with a whole grain and you’ve got a complete meal full of lean protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates that is sure to be a crowd pleaser.
ingredients: 3 stalks green onion (scallion) (white and light green parts chopped)
12 oz boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 small head broccoli (cut into bite-sized pieces (~2 cups))
6 whole California dates (pitted and thinly sliced)
2 tbsp fresh lime juice (from 1 med lime)
steps: In a wok or high-sided sauté pan over medium-high heat, add oil, ginger, garlic, and scallions and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add red pepper flakes and chicken and cook for about 4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add bell pepper and broccoli to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, 2–3 minutes.

Add chicken back to the pan as well as rice vinegar, soy sauce, and dates. Mix well throughout the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low and bring the liquid to a simmer and reduce until thicker or more syrupy. If a thinner sauce is desired, add 2–4 tablespoons of water. Allow to simmer for about 5 minutes.
Remove pan from heat. Mix in cilantro, basil, and lime juice. Garnish with toasted cashews.
Optional: Serve with brown rice or another grain.
Note: You can swap out the bell pepper and/or broccoli for other vegetables.

title: Zucchini and Fresh Corn Succotash
description: Cook fresh corn on the cob for this recipe by simmering it in boiling water for 8 minutes. Let the ears of corn cool, and then use a sharp knife to cut the kernels off the cob.
ingredients: 4 med ears corn (fresh, cooked and kernels cut off the cob)
steps: Add the olive oil to a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 5-6 minutes or until the onions start to turn clear.
Add the garlic and zucchini and sauté for 4-5 more minutes until the zucchini is just starting to soften.
Add the corn and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Then add remaining ingredients until heated through.

title: Strawberries, 1/2 cup
description: Nutrition information for 1/2 cup of strawberries

title: Radish & Watermelon Arugula Salad
description: Impress your guests with this diabetes-friendly Radish and Watermelon Arugula Salad. This great summer salad showcases sweet watermelon with peppery radishes, crunchy onions, and a tangy dressing.
serving_size: 2 cups arugula, 1 cup watermelon radish mixture
ingredients: 1 small seedless watermelon (diced, about 3 ½–4 cups)
1 bunch radish (stems cut away and thinly sliced)
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the vinegar, salt, pepper, olive oil, and mint.
In a large bowl, combine the watermelon, onion, radishes, and feta cheese.
Add dressing and stir gently to combine. Serve on a bed of baby arugula.

title: Raspberries, 1 cup
description: Nutrition information for Raspberries

title: Garlicky Ginger Eggplant
description:
This asian-inspired vegetable dish features eggplant, mushrooms, and bean sprouts in a garlic-ginger hoisin sauce. The recipe calls for Chinese or Japanese eggplant, which is long and skinny. If you can't find Chinese eggplant, you can sub in regular eggplant and chop into 1-inch cubes. This could be a side dish or a vegetarian main dish. Add tofu or other plant-based protein source for a complete vegetarian meal.

Powered by Homemade, brought to you by Davita.
steps: Heat sesame oil in a large skillet. Add eggplant, ginger, garlic, mushrooms and bean sprouts. Stir-fry over medium-high heat until eggplant begins to soften, 4-6 minutes.
Add basil, chili pepper flakes and hoisin sauce to eggplant. Continue cooking for 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat and serve.

title: Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri
description: Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri is a flavorful and satisfying vegetarian dish that transforms cauliflower into hearty steaks and pairs them with a vibrant, zesty chimichurri sauce.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp ground red pepper flakes (adjust to taste)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Remove the outer leaves from the cauliflower heads. Trim the stem end to create a flat base.
Cut each cauliflower head into 1-inch-thick slices to create cauliflower steaks.
Place the cauliflower steaks on a baking sheet. Brush both sides with 1 Tbsp olive oil and season with kosher salt and black pepper.
Roast the cauliflower steaks until golden brown and tender, about 20 minutes.

While the cauliflower is roasting, prepare the chimichurri sauce. In a bowl, combine the finely chopped parsley, cilantro, minced garlic, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, red wine vinegar, extra-virgin olive oil, kosher salt and black pepper. Whisk until well-combined.
Once the cauliflower steaks are done, transfer them to serving plates.
Spoon chimichurri sauce generously over each cauliflower steak.

title: Roasted Beet, Apple and Queso Fresco Salad
description: A delicious salad that lets you include some fall produce like beets.
ingredients: 2 cup Golden Delicious apples (peeled and cubed (1/2-inch cubes))
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Rub canola oil on beets, making sure to cover the whole surface. Pierce a few holes in beets so heat can circulate and speed up the cooking process. Place beets in a small baking dish and cover tightly with foil. Roast beets for 1 hour 10 minutes, until you can easily pierce the flesh of the beet with a fork. Remove from oven and place beets directly into a bowl with ice water. This will cool down the beets rapidly, stop the cooking process, and make removing the skins that much easier. When beets are cooled, peel off skins with a paper towel. Put beets into 1/2-inch cubes and set aside.
Add avocado oil, lime juice, salt, and black pepper to a bowl and whisk briskly for 30 seconds to create your dressing. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, add apples, 2 cups beet cubes, cilantro, queso fresco, and onions, and toss gently. Add dressing and toss once more. Now it’s ready to serve. Enjoy!

title: Italian Beans and Greens Salad
description: Beans and greens is a classic Italian meal or side dish. In this diabetes-friendly version, the cured ham is replaced with turkey bacon and chicken sausage. They are mixed with baby greens and cannellini beans and made into a salad. It’s a hearty, fresh twist on a mediterranean classic.
serving_size: 1 cup salad greens + 1 oz. chicken sausage
ingredients: 2 slice turkey bacon (cut into ½ inch pieces)
2 whole Italian seasoned chicken sausages (cut into ½ -inch rounds)
1/2 cup low sodium cannellini beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: In a large skillet, cook the turkey bacon until crispy and sausage until browned.
Place greens, cannellini beans, and onions in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, garlic, and black pepper together. Drizzle over the salad and toss to coat the greens. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

title: Tomato and Zucchini Salsa
description: This tomato and zucchini salsa is a versatile and nutritious option that celebrates the flavors of fresh, seasonal produce. Enjoy its crisp texture and vibrant taste as a delightful addition to your meals or as a standalone snack.
ingredients: 1 small jalapeño pepper (seeded and finely minced)
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the diced tomatoes, diced zucchini, finely chopped red onion, chopped cilantro, and minced jalapeño pepper. Add the minced garlic to the mixture. Drizzle the fresh lime juice over the ingredients. Season the salsa with salt and pepper.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until they are well mixed and coated with the lime juice and seasonings.
Let the salsa sit for about 10–15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together. Adjust the seasoning to suit your preference

title: Honey, Vanilla, and Raspberry Yogurt Popsicles
description: These Honey, Vanilla and Raspberry Yogurt Popsicles are a creamy way to cool down. Diabetes-friendly, they are a kid-approved dessert that’s perfect in the summer.
steps: In a blender, puree yogurt and raspberries.
Once blended, drizzle the honey and vanilla into the mix. Blend thoroughly.
Pour the mixture into popsicle molds. Freeze for 8 hours or overnight.

title: Lemony Pesto Hummus
description: Enjoy this hummus as a dip for snacking with non-starchy vegetables, whole-wheat pita, or whole-grain crackers.
ingredients: 1 (14.5 oz) can chickpeas (garbanzo beans) (drained and rinsed)
steps: Add all ingredients to a food processor or blender and blend until smooth.

title: Spinach, Avocado, and Summer Berry Salad
description: This superfood salad is packed with antioxidants and bright, summery flavors. Pair it with a grilled chicken dish, like these Grilled Lime Chicken Fajitas, or fish, like this Grilled Salmon with Mango and Tomato Salsa. Looking for an easier way to make salad dressing? Add all of the dressing ingredients to a jar with a lid. Screw the lid on tightly and shake well until everything is combined. If you're making this salad ahead of time, wait to add the dressing until right before serving.
ingredients: 1/3 cup finely diced or sliced red onion
2 tbsp white balsamic or champagne vinegar
steps: Place the spinach, strawberries, blueberries, avocado, and onion in a large salad bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, honey, lime juice, garlic, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to evenly coat.

title: Turkey and Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Turn your appetizer game up a notch with our Turkey and Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms—a savory symphony that transforms ordinary cremini mushrooms into bite-sized wonders. These little powerhouses feature cremini mushrooms cradling a lively mix of fresh spinach, lean ground turkey, and a touch of Parmesan, ensuring a diabetes-friendly twist on a classic.
ingredients: 16 large cremini (baby bella) mushrooms (cleaned and stems removed)
steps: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F and prepare a baking sheet by lining it with parchment paper or lightly greasing it with cooking spray.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the lean ground turkey, breaking it into small pieces, until it's browned and fully cooked. Drain any excess fat.
In the same skillet, add finely diced onion and minced garlic, and sauté for 2–3 minutes until they become fragrant and slightly softened.
Add the chopped fresh spinach to the skillet and cook for another 2–3 minutes until it wilts and any excess moisture evaporates.
Stir in the grated Parmesan cheese, dried oregano and rosemary. Season the mixture with salt and pepper. Mix well and let it cool slightly.
Take the cleaned mushrooms and lightly brush or spray them with cooking spray or olive oil. Arrange them on the prepared baking sheet with the gill side up.
Fill each mushroom cap with the turkey and spinach mixture, pressing it down slightly to pack it in.
Bake the stuffed mushrooms in the preheated oven for about 15–20 minutes or until the mushrooms are tender, and the filling is heated through and slightly browned.
Remove the stuffed mushrooms from the oven and allow them to cool for a few minutes before serving.

title: Cinnamon Roasted Pears
description: Fruit is a great end to a meal. By experimenting with roasting and grilling fruit, you can bring out its maximum flavor. This recipe could easily be made with apples too.
ingredients: 2 medium Anjou Pears ((about 6.5 ounces each) peeled, cored and sliced in half)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a small bowl (using fingers) combine margarine, cinnamon and brown sugar. Add walnuts and mix.
Arrange the pears cut side up in an 8-inch square glass baking dish. Pour 1/4 cup water in bottom of pan.
Divide the brown sugar mixture evenly among the pear halves and place in middle of pears.
Bake until the pears are tender and beginning to brown, about 45 minutes.

title: Vegetarian Baked Beans
description: You can make these baked beans with pinto beans if you prefer them over navy beans.
ingredients: 2 (14.5-oz) cans navy or great northern beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Coat an 8-inch baking pan with cooking spray. Set aside.
Mix all the ingredients in a large bowl. Pour into prepared baking pan. Cover and bake for 45 minutes. Uncover and bake an additional 30 to 40 minutes or until thickened.

title: Cucumber and Radish Salad
description: Love the flavors of fresh veggies? Then give this cucumber and radish salad a taste! Paired with fresh herbs and an easy salad dressing, it’s a great appetizer or side salad for any meal needing a bit more color.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the thinly sliced cucumbers, radishes, red onion, chopped fresh dill, and fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together the white wine vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the cucumber, radish, and herb mixture.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.
Allow the salad to marinate in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes to enhance the flavors.

title: Budget-Friendly Greek Salad and Grilled Shrimp Pitas
description: Serve this dish with a cup of cold gazpacho soup or with sautéed zucchini seasoned with lemon juice and oregano.
ingredients: 1/2 large, or 1 small cucumber(s) (peeled and sliced)
steps: Prepare an indoor or outdoor grill.
In a large bowl, toss together lettuce, onion, cucumber, feta cheese, olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano.
Fill each pita pocket half with 1/4 of lettuce mixture. Set aside.
Season shrimp with salt (optional), ground black pepper and cayenne pepper. Spray shrimp with cooking spray.
Grill shrimp for 3-4 minutes on each side. Remove from grill and add 3 shrimp to each pita.

title: Garden Harvest Soup
description: Adjust the veggies in this soup based on what you have in your refrigerator. Get creative with the veggie combination that you use!
ingredients: 2 cup vegetables (uncooked, chopped, such as any combination of bell peppers, carrots, green beans, yellow summer squash, or zucchini)
2 cup low sodium chicken broth (low-sodium vegetable broth or fat-free, low-sodium)
1 cup fresh spinach leaves (loosely packed, coarsely chopped)
steps: In a medium saucepan, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook the 2 cups chopped vegetables, onion, and seasoning blend for 8 to 10 minutes, or until tender-crisp, stirring occasionally. (If the vegetables get dry or start to scorch, add a little water to the saucepan.)

Stir in the broth. Increase the heat to medium high and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes so the flavors blend, stirring occasionally. Stir in the spinach. Sprinkle each serving with Parmesan cheese.

Tips: Chop firmer vegetables, such as carrots, into smaller pieces than more tender vegetables, such as zucchini, so all the vegetables will cook at about the same rate. If you want this dish to be vegetarian, be sure to use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.

title: Whole Wheat Fresh Gingerbread
description: This fresh gingerbread loaf is a wholesome twist on a classic favorite, offering the warm, spicy notes of ginger and molasses, but with the goodness of whole wheat flour. It's a delightful addition to your holiday spread that the whole family is sure to enjoy! This diabetes-friendly is a great option to bring to a holiday cookie swap or to serve at your holiday meal to celebrate the season.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, brown sugar substitute, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves.
In another bowl, combine the applesauce, maple syrup, vegetable oil, freshly grated ginger, eggs, and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined.
Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, stirring until just combined. Do not overmix.
Slowly pour in the hot water while gently stirring the batter. The batter will be thin.
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 45–50 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the bread comes out clean.
Once baked, remove the gingerbread from the oven and allow it to cool in the pan for about 10 minutes. Then, carefully remove it from the pan and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Cold Cucumber Soup and Grilled Shrimp Open-Face Sandwich
description: Cool as a cucumber, this refreshing soup pairs perfectly with a grilled shrimp and spicy avocado aioli open-face sandwich. If the spice is too much, you can skip the hot sauce or just use a dash.
ingredients: 2 med cucumber(s) (cut in thirds and in half lengthwise)
4 tbsp lemon juice (from 2 med lemons, divided)
steps: To make the soup, place half of the cucumbers in a food processor fit with the chopping blade. Process until it is cut into small pieces. Add the remaining cucumber sections and process until they are cut into small pieces.
Add the yogurt, lemon juice, lemon zest, and dill and process until liquified and all cucumber pieces are puréed.

Spray a grill pan or outdoor grill with cooking spray and heat to medium. Toss the shrimp with olive oil and black pepper. Place on the preheated grill and cook for 1 minute. Flip the shrimp and cook for an additional minute. Shrimp cooks quickly, so be careful not to overcook it. Remove it from the grill to a plate.
In a small bowl, mash the avocado and add the mayonnaise, lemon juice, and hot sauce, and mix until light green in color and the avocado is incorporated and smooth.
Spread 1 Tbsp of the avocado aioli over each slice of toast. Top with ¼ cup of arugula and 3 shrimp. Serve with 1 ¼ cup of the soup on the side.

title: Sheet Pan Tofu Fajitas
description: Sheet pan dinners are a quick and easy way to enjoy a nutritious meal without a lot of clean up. This diabetes-friendly tofu fajitas meal is one the whole family will love and uses plant-based protein to keep you full and satisfied.
ingredients: 16 oz extra firm tofu (pressed and cubed)
4 whole low carb whole wheat burrito wraps
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Press the tofu to remove excess water, then cut it into cubes.
In a large bowl, combine tofu cubes, sliced bell peppers, and sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, taco seasoning, ground cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, and black pepper to create the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the tofu and vegetables. Toss until everything is evenly coated. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Spread the marinated tofu and vegetables evenly on the sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the tofu is golden and the vegetables are tender, stirring halfway through.
Divide the fajita filling among the wraps.
Serve the sheet pan tofu fajitas and garnish with chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Salad Bar Gazpacho Salad
description: This tasty salad uses a light tomato-based dressing and is packed with greens and other nutrient-rich veggies. Buy as many of these vegetables as you can precut from your grocer’s salad bar to save on prep time.
ingredients: 2 cup chickpeas, red kidney beans, or black beans (from salad bar or canned, drained and rinsed)
steps: Combine the beans, tomato, corn, cucumber, red onion, and cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together the tomato juice, lime juice, olive oil, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Pour over the salad and mix gently. Serve over the mixed greens.

title: Sweet Potato Salad
description: Who says you can only use white potatoes for a potato salad? This dish will be a welcomed surprise at your next summer picnic.
steps: Peel sweet potatoes and cube. Place sweet potatoes in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Boil until tender about 5-7 minutes. Drain potatoes and rinse with cold water; let cool.
While potatoes are cooking, cook bacon until crisp, then chop or crumble into small pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk together, olive oil, apple cider vinegar, pepper and garlic powder.
Place sweet potatoes in serving bowl and add celery, green onions and turkey bacon. Pour dressing over salad and toss until potatoes are coated. Serve cold.

title: Mango Mango Salad with Chicken
description: Traditional chicken salad is made a little more lively with the addition of mango! Find this recipe and more in The New Soul Food Cookbook for People with Diabetes.
ingredients: 1 med green bell pepper (seeded and chopped)
steps: Combine the mayonnaise and green onions in a small bowl, cover, and chill. Combine the chicken, mango, and bell pepper in a large bowl.
Combine the vinegar, lemon juice, and sugar in a container with a tight lid. Shake well. Add lemon mixture to the mayonnaise and green onion mixture and stir well.
Pour the dressing over the chicken and mango, toss well, and chill for 30 minutes. To serve, spoon onto a plate lined with lettuce leaves.

title: Crispy Potato Taco Bowl
description: This taco bowl features a hearty base of roasted white potatoes and fluffy cauliflower rice topped with savory ground beef, mushrooms, and red bell peppers. Fresh lime juice and cilantro brighten every bite, while creamy avocado adds richness and balance. It’s a satisfying, veggie-packed, high-fiber twist on classic taco flavors that’s easy enough for weeknights and perfect for build-your-own bowls.
ingredients: 12 oz white potatoes (about 2 medium, diced into 1/2-inch cubes)
1 cup red bell pepper (about 1 medium pepper, diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Toss diced potatoes with 1 1/2 tsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender and lightly browned.

In the same skillet, heat the remaining 1 1/2 tsp olive oil over medium heat. Add ground beef, chopped mushrooms, and diced red bell pepper. Cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking apart the beef, until meat is fully cooked and vegetables are tender.

Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato sauce and water and bring to a simmer. Bring to a boil then reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the liquid is reduced. Remove from heat.

While the beef mixture is simmering, heat cauliflower rice in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally until heated through. Add the cilantro and lime juice and mix together. Keep warm until ready to serve.
Divide the cauliflower rice evenly among four bowls. Top each bowl evenly with roasted potatoes, beef-mushroom-pepper mixture, two tomatoes, and 1/4 of a sliced avocado.

title: Kid-Friendly Rainbow Fruit Platter
description: A quick, easy, and colorful recipe that anyone can make! Try it as breakfast, a snack, or even dessert.
ingredients: 1 fresh pineapple (peeled, cored, and cubed (about 4 cups))
steps: Mix the yogurt and chia seeds. Refrigerate overnight. Mix in 1/8 tsp cinnamon.
On a very large platter, place the strawberries in the top row to form the top of a rainbow pattern.
Place the cantaloupe cubes as the second row below the strawberries. Continue this process with the pineapple, going through the blackberries, to make the rainbow pattern.

title: Korean BBQ-Inspired Baked Salmon
description: The Korean BBQ-inspired sauce on this salmon has that ideal balance of sweet, salty, tangy, and spicy. The sweetness comes naturally from fruit, not added sugars. You could also use this sauce on chicken: bake boneless, skinless chicken thighs without the sauce for 15 minutes, then brush on the sauce and bake for another 15 minutes, or until cooked through.
ingredients: 4 (6-oz) fillets center-cut sockeye salmon with skin
1 tbsp reduced-sodium tamari or soy sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the salmon, skin side down, on the baking sheet.

In a small bowl, stir together the ketchup, jam, tamari, vinegar, and hot pepper sauce. Lightly spread the mixture onto the top of each fillet using the back of the spoon. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake until the salmon is flaky and cooked through (with an internal temperature of at least 145°F), about 16 minutes. Serve.

title: Shrimp Sauté with Spinach, Grape Tomatoes, and Roasted Red Potatoes
description: This quick and delicious shrimp dish follows the Low Carb and Low Fat Eating Pattern, meaning it’s a good choice for people who are mindful of their blood pressure. Succulent shrimp are sautéed with fresh spinach, sweet grape tomatoes, and crispy roasted red potatoes, creating a harmonious blend of flavors and textures. It's a hearty and flavorful dish that's perfect for a weeknight dinner.
serving_size: 1 cup shrimp and veggies, ½ cup potatoes
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Halve or quarter the baby red potatoes, depending on their size. Toss them with 2 tsp olive oil, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast in the oven for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway through, until golden and tender.

Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining olive oil and grape tomatoes to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3–4 minutes, or until the tomatoes soften and release some of their juices
Add the garlic, shrimp, and crushed red pepper to the skillet. Sauté the shrimp for 1–2 minutes per side, or until opaque and cooked through.
Add the spinach to the skillet in handfuls, stirring after each addition to allow it to wilt.
Reduce the heat to low and sprinkle half the grated Parmesan cheese over the skillet contents. Stir to combine, allowing the cheese to melt slightly.
Divide the shrimp, sautéed veggies, and spinach between plates. Garnish with the reserved Parmesan cheese and basil ribbons. Serve alongside the roasted red potatoes.

title: Broccoli Onion Latkes
description: The low carb latkes use broccoli instead of the traditional potatoes. They are also lower in potassium, making them a great alternative for those following a low potassium diet for kidney health.
ingredients: 3 cup fresh or frozen chopped broccoli florets
steps: Boil the diced broccoli in a small amount of water for 5 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
Break eggs into a medium bowl and beat. Add the flour and mix well. Add the broccoli and onion and stir into the flour/egg mixture until well mixed.

Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Drop the mixture by spoonfuls into the hot oil, making 4 equal portions. Flatten with a spatula, and cook until golden brown on both sides (about 3-4 minutes per side).
Remove the latkes from the pan and drain on a paper towel to soak up extra oil. Serve hot.

title: Besan Chilla
description: Made with chickpea flour and colorful vegetables, besan chilla is a popular savory pancake enjoyed in many Indian households. Its lightly nutty flavor, crisp edges, and tender center make it a tasty snack or light meal, while the chickpea flour provides protein and fiber.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the besan, water, and spices until smooth.
Stir in the vegetables. Cover and set aside for 5-10 minutes. Mix well again.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly coat with cooking spray.
Pour the batter into the skillet, gently spread the batter evenly, and round off the shape to create a thin, 6-inch pancake.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through.
Serve warm with 1 Tbsp plain Greek yogurt on the side for dipping.

title: Nutritional Yeast
description: Nutrition information for 4 tbsp of nutritional yeast.

title: Creamy Mashed Cauliflower
description: Creamy Mashed Cauliflower is a low carb alternative for when you are craving mashed potatoes. This diabetes-friendly recipe is everything you could want out of a classic comfort food dish.
steps: Steam or boil the cauliflower florets until they are fork-tender, about 10–12 minutes.
Add the cook cauliflower to a large bowl.
In a small pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the garlic butter, salt, and pepper to the cauliflower.
Add Greek yogurt to the cauliflower.
Use a hand blender to blend the cauliflower until smooth and creamy.

title: Creamy Chicken Apple Salad
description: This salad is a low-carb, power-food dynamo. Easy to prepare and packed full of good nutrition—protein from chicken, fiber from the apple, and healthy fat from the walnuts—this is a quick diabetes-friendly recipe that's perfect for lunches and making ahead. Full of flavor and crunch—you won’t believe how easy it is!
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, celery, green onions, apple, and walnuts
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper. Pour over the chicken mixture and gently stir to coat.
Serve salad over your choice of lettuce leaves, bread or crackers.

title: Sweet Potato Salad with Cilantro and Lime
description: This Tex-Mex style salad is hearty and filling and sure to rev up your taste buds. It’s diabetes-friendly and would work great as a side dish for your next taco Tuesday dinner!
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into bite-sized cubes)
1 (15 oz) can black beans (Reduced sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a large bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Spread the seasoned sweet potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
While the sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare the dressing. Zest and juice the lime. In a small bowl, combine chopped fresh cilantro, lime zest, and lime juice.
Once the sweet potatoes are done, transfer them to a serving bowl.
Pour the cilantro and lime dressing over the roasted sweet potatoes.
Add finely chopped red onion, avocado, and black beans to the bowl.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.

title: Cauliflower Tabbouleh
description: Tabbouleh is a traditional mediterranean salad made with flavorful herbs, fresh lemon, and couscous. This diabetes-friendly version uses cauliflower rice for lower carb, grain-free alternative.
ingredients: 1 head small head cauliflower (or 16-oz frozen cauliflower rice) (leaves and stem removed)
steps: Mince the parsley and mint leaves (or grind in a food processor) and add to a large bowl.
Grate the cauliflower using a box grater and stir together with the parsley and mint.
Add the diced tomato and stir it into the salad.
Drizzle the salad with the olive oil and lemon juice, and sprinkle with the salt (optional) and black pepper. Stir to coat.
Cover and let the tabbouleh marinate for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Easy Middle Eastern Green Beans
description:
This dish is inspired by a Lebanese dish called loubieh. It’s simply green beans and grape tomatoes cooked with a just-right amount of extra-virgin olive oil and seasoned with cinnamon and sea salt. It comes together quickly and can easily be made while the rest of your meal cooks. Pair it with a simple protein dish, like this Balsamic Glazed Salmon, for a quick and easy weeknight dinner.

Find this recipe and more in The Clean & Simple Diabetes Cookbook by Jackie Newgent, RDN, CDN
ingredients: 8 oz fresh green beans (stem ends trimmed)
steps: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the green beans and tomatoes, cover, and cook until the green beans are tender yet crisp and the tomatoes are fully softened, about 10 minutes. Toss with tongs a couple of times throughout the cooking.
Sprinkle the vegetables with the cinnamon and salt. Toss to combine, and then serve.

title: Whole-Wheat Spinach Parathas
description: Paratha is a type of flatbread that originated in the northern part of India, where it is still popular. It’s part of a traditional Indian breakfast, but can also be served alongside lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 2 cups plus 1 tbsp whole-wheat pastry flour (divided)
1 whole green chile (seeds discarded, finely minced)
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat 1 tsp oil over medium-high heat. Add the ajwain seeds, gingerroot, and chile. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring frequently.

Add the spinach and ¼ tsp salt. Cook for 3 minutes, or until the moisture released from the spinach is absorbed and the base becomes dry. Add the amchoor powder and cumin, stirring well. Remove from the heat. Set aside to cool.

To make the dough for the paratha: mix 2 cups flour and the remaining ¼ tsp salt in a shallow dish. Add the spinach mixture to the flour mixture. Add water, little by little, to form a smooth dough (similar to the consistency of a pizza dough). Knead the dough until smooth. Transfer to a glass bowl. Cover with a damp towel. Set aside for 30 minutes to an hour at room temperature.

After the standing time, knead the dough once again. Shape into 8 balls. Lightly dust your work surface with the remaining 1 Tbsp flour. Using a rolling pin, flatten each dough ball so it’s 6 inches in diameter.
Preheat a cast iron griddle or flat skillet over medium-high heat. Place one piece of dough in the skillet. Cook for about 1 minute, or until it begins to bubble.

Turn the paratha. Brush with ¼ tsp of the remaining oil. Continue cooking for about 3–4 minutes per side, turning as necessary, until the edges are brown on both sides. Using a flat spatula, press the middle of the paratha as it’s cooking so it cooks evenly.
Remove from the skillet. Repeat the cooking process with the remaining pieces of dough and remaining oil. Serve hot.

title: Caprese Kabobs
description: This easy appetizer is perfect for summer and uses garden fresh ingredients. These kabobs are packed with flavor and low in carbohydrates. They also look beautiful on a serving platter and are sure to impress guests!
ingredients: 18 whole fresh mozzarella balls (1/4 ounce each)
steps: Place 1 grape tomato, 1 basil leaf, and 1 mozzarella ball on each bamboo fork. Repeat this process for 18 kabobs. Place the kabobs on a serving platter.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Right before serving, drizzle the dressing over the kabobs to coat evenly.

title: Blood Orange Salad (Insalata D’ Arrance Sangouse)
description: Sicily is known for its beautiful, lush orange groves, which produce some of the world’s most fragrant oranges. First introduced by the Arabs during their rule of the island, orange trees flourished in the ashes along the base of Mt. Etna. Look for the sweetest oranges possible for this recipe. If you can, use Sicilian blood oranges; their red color imparts festive flair to this sumptuous salad.
ingredients: 4 whole blood oranges (about 1 pound total, peeled and sliced into rounds)
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (preferably first cold-pressed and unfiltered)
steps: Place orange slices on a large platter and scatter green onions over the top.
In a small bowl, whisk orange juice and olive oil together, and season with salt, pepper, and crushed red chile flakes. Drizzle over the salad, and serve immediately.

title: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip
description: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip is a light and creamy alternative to traditional dips, providing a protein-packed option for snacking. Enjoy with your favorite veggies like broccoli, bell pepper, carrots, and more!
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine the low-fat cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, fresh lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and minced garlic. Blend the ingredients until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. This may take a few minutes, depending on the power of your blender or food processor.
Once the mixture is smooth, transfer it to a bowl. Stir in the chopped fresh chives and season the whipped cottage cheese dip with pepper. Mix well to ensure the flavors are evenly distributed.
Refrigerate the dip for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld and enhance the overall taste.

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Whip up a hearty and flavorful dish that's sure to satisfy your cravings while helping to keep your blood glucose (blood sugar) levels in check. Learn step-by-step how to create a creamy, savory sauce paired with lean beef and wholesome ingredients, making this dish both delicious and mindful of your health. Whether you're cooking for yourself or your loved ones, this recipe is sure to become a staple in your kitchen.
ingredients: 1 lbs beef tenderloin (0" trim, sliced into 2-inch strips)
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions, omitting salt.
Add oil to a large sauté pan over high heat. Add meat and sauté for about 3 minutes. Remove meat from pan. Add mushrooms and onion and sauté for 5 minutes or until it begins to brown.
Add flour and cook for 1 minute. Add water gently to deglaze pan; cook for 2 minutes. Add Dijon mustard and beef broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add beef and any juices back to broth and simmer for 3 more minutes. Add sour cream and pepper; simmer for 30 seconds.
Serve over whole-grain egg noodles.

title: Healthy Snack Mix—Foodie Recipe
description: This snack mix is packed with nutrition and healthy fats from the many nuts and seeds. Plus the freeze-dried blueberries add a tangy, fruity flavor to the mix!
steps: Preheat an oven to 300 degrees F.
Coat a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
In a bowl, combine the brown sugar substitute, cayenne pepper, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, almonds and sesame seeds. Toss to coat.
Spread mixture onto the baking sheet and then spray again with a light coating of cooking spray.
Bake for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to ensure even browning.
Remove from oven and set aside to cool. When cool, toss the nut mixture in a bowl with the freeze-dried blueberries.

title: Savory Seaweed Edamame Yogurt Bowl
description: This savory yogurt bowl brings together creamy nonfat Greek yogurt, tender edamame, and the salty crunch of roasted seaweed for a high-protein, flavor-packed snack. It’s quick, refreshing, and delivers a sushi-inspired twist without any cooking.
steps: Add 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt to a small bowl.
Stir in 1/2 cup shelled edamame until evenly distributed.
Crumble the pack of roasted seaweed over the top or fold it in for a softer texture.
Serve immediately so the seaweed stays crisp.

title: Black Bean Patties with Cilantro and Lime
description: Looking for a light summer burger? These black bean patties are delicious on a whole-grain bun, over a salad or simply on a plate with sliced onions.
ingredients: 1 can low sodium black beans (16-ounce can, do not drain)
1/4 cup, plus additional for dusting cornmeal (yellow or white)
1/4 cup cheddar cheese (reduced-fat, or use reduced-fat pepper Jack cheese)
1 spray, 0.25g nonstick cooking spray (for scoop or measuring cup)
steps: In a large nonstick pan heat olive oil and sauté onions, peppers, garlic, and spices. Sauté for 3 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.

Add black beans with liquid and sauté with vegetables for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Add breadcrumbs, cornmeal, lime juice, lime zest, and salt. Remove 1 cup of bean mixture and purée in a blender or food processor until a coarse purée is formed. Fold the purée back into the bean mixture. Add the cheddar cheese and cilantro, combine well. Mixture should resemble a coarse paste and be stiff enough to hold up in a scoop or spoon.

With an ice cream scoop or 1/3 cup measuring cup, form 3–4-ounce portions. (Spray the ice cream scoop or measuring cup lightly with cooking spray to make it easier to remove the mixture) Sprinkle a plate with cornmeal and place scooped black bean portions on plate. Lightly dust black bean mixture with cornmeal and press down gently, forming a patty.

Preheat oven to 375°F. Spray a large nonstick pan with vegetable oil. Brown patty cakes for 2 minutes on each side. If pan is ovenproof, transfer to oven and bake for 15 minutes or until heated through. Or transfer patty cakes to a cookie sheet pan and bake.

title: Cherry Oat Crisp
description: Cherry Oat Crisp is a delightful dessert that combines sweet and tart cherries with a crunchy oat topping. This healthier version is diabetes-friendly so everyone can enjoy.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a 9 x 9-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the pitted cherries, lemon juice, zero-calorie maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Toss until the cherries are well coated.
Add the cherries to the prepared baking dish and spread in an even layer.
In a separate bowl, mix the oats, almond flour, chopped nuts, vegetable oil, and salt. Stir until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture evenly over the top of the cherries.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until the cherry filling is bubbly, and the oat topping is golden brown.
Let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm.

title: Smoky Black Bean Dip
description: Dive into flavor paradise with our Smoky Black Bean Dip, a zesty sensation that transforms ordinary black beans into a smoky fiesta. Serve this dip with some fresh veggies for a healthy, low-carb snack or appetizer that’s perfect for people with and without diabetes.
serving_size: 1/4 cup dip + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber and bell pepper
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans (No added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: Use a food processor to combine the drained and rinsed black beans, minced garlic, chopped fresh cilantro, lime juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Blend until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You can gradually drizzle in 1 tablespoon of olive oil while blending to create your desired texture. Feel free to adjust the amount of oil according to your preference.
After blending, taste the dip and make any necessary adjustments to the seasonings. You can add more salt, pepper, or lime juice to suit your taste.
Transfer the black bean dip to a serving bowl and gently swirl in 2 tablespoons of plain Greek yogurt. This addition provides a creamy element and a touch of tanginess to the dip.
Serve with sliced cucumbers and bell peppers.

title: Grilled Portabellas with Tomato and Tuscan Herbs
description: These delicious mushrooms make a flavorful sandwich topped with a slice of fresh mozzarella or provolone and served on whole grain bread. Serve a mixed green salad on the side.
ingredients: 6 whole Portobello mushrooms (wiped clean and stem removed)
steps: Combine all of the marinade ingredients in a medium bowl and put into a large tightly sealed plastic bag. Marinate mushroom caps at least 15-30 minutes at room temperature for best results.

Preheat grill to medium high and place mushroom caps on grill grate. Cook under direct heat for 5 minutes per side until completely through to tender. Baste occasionally with additional marinade while cooking. You can pour any leftover marinade over mushrooms before serving.
